answer: Require each identity to train a small model on its own assigned data slice, then publish its weights in a public vault for re-testing. A copied model is only an echo of another identity\’s work: checks split the claim into facets — accuracy on held-out data, fit to the slice, and training cost — so the echo fails one facet. The voyage from slice to weights takes real time, like growing a cedar. A sybil farmer pays GPU-hours per fake, so ten thousand clones cost ten thousand times as much. Limit: cheap rentals blunt the price, and verification costs compute, so spot-checks should sample.
